**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – no documented first-touch-to-first-class sequence; risk of inconsistent induction, missed health screening, unclear expectations on gym use/etiquette
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no retention trigger or win-back playbook; losing members without understanding why or attempting recovery
- **Member Checkins** – no cadence or framework for engagement touchpoints (week 1, month 1, 3, 6); critical for retention signal
- **Member Pause** – no SOP for freeze requests; unclear terms, duration, re-engagement protocol
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – no progression framework for coaches; unclear how they level up, get certified, or move into lead/senior roles
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no mechanism to standardise class delivery or catch coaching drift
- **Health & Safety incident response** – not listed; must have escalation protocol, injury reporting, safeguarding
- **Member data privacy & GDPR** – regulatory gap; no documented data retention, consent, access, deletion workflow
- **Order Supplies & Sundries** – no reorder triggers or accountability; risk of stockouts or waste
- **Referral Programme** – no mechanics documented; how members earn, redeem, track
- **Finance reconciliation** – "General" area has 1/1 SOP; unclear what's covered; likely missing cash handling, refunds, disputed charges, pricing changes

**Needs updating**

- **Member Outcomes** SOP – likely vague; needs to define what "outcome" means (strength, endurance, confidence, body comp?), measurement method, tracking cadence, coach accountability
- **30 Day Goals** – needs tie-in to onboarding; unclear if this is coach-led or self-serve, how it's logged, reviewed

# Service Menu Build - Execution Plan for Grace

• **Start with your revenue reality, not your wishlist.** Audit last 3 months: What are members actually *buying*?* What generates 80% of revenue? Build the menu around those winners first, then add 2-3 adjacent offerings. This stops menu bloat that confuses both coaches and members.

• **Create two *different* documents, not one.** Members see: class packages + pricing + what's included (duration, cancellation, freezes). Coaches see: *how to sell it* (commission structure, upsell triggers, objection handling). A coach needs to know "if someone says they can't commit to 12 months, here's the 6-month alternative." Members don't need that complexity.

• **Price in tiers, not à la carte.** Offer 3 clear entry points (e.g., "Starter 4 classes/month," "Core Unlimited," "VIP 1:1 sessions"). This forces decision-making and stops the sales conversations dying in paradox of choice. Test pricing against local competitors *once* — then own your positioning.

• **Get it on the wall and in a 1-page PDF by end of week.** Print it. Have coaches use it with the next 10 inquiries and gather feedback. You'll spot what's confusing in real conversations, not in theory. Iterate after those 10 sales, not before.

• **Link it to your booking system immediately.** If it lives in a Google Doc only, it'll be outdated by next month. Make buying/booking the same action for members.

July was an anomaly—you hit 215 leads at £2/lead with a 13.5% close rate (29 sales). August collapsed to 109 leads at £5/lead despite higher spend, and close rate held at 22% (actually your strongest conversion). This isn't a creative or messaging problem; the lead *quality* tanked in August while the sales quality stayed solid. Something changed in your targeting, audience, or ad setup between July and August that widened your funnel to cheaper, colder prospects who don't convert.

Your profit-per-sale in August (£52) is strong, but you're now getting half the volume at 2.5× the cost-per-lead. April–June showed cost-per-lead drift (£6→£21) before the July reset, suggesting you've hit this ceiling before when audiences fatigue or targeting gets too broad.

The 22% close rate is excellent for a gym trial lead and means your sales team or follow-up is working. Don't fix what isn't broken there.

Check: audience size, age/location breakdowns, interest/behaviour stacks, lookalike seed, and placement mix. **Trend:** July's £19,764 is your best month (excluding April relocation spike). But churn spiked to 12.8% in May — you lost 17 members that month — and only recovered to 140 active by July. That's fragile growth.

- **Fix churn first.** May's 12.8% is 3× your best months (3.4–3.5%). Identify what happened in April/May (post-move friction? summer holidays? billing issues?). Target: return to <4% by September. At 12.8% churn, you're burning £1,900+ in annual member value monthly.
- **Pricing gap.** Rev/member ranges £118–£141; July hit £141 but Feb-Jun averaged £124. You're leaving £15–20/month per member on the table. Test a tiered membership or add class packs (intro, power, unlimited) — you have the space now post-relocation. Conservative uplift: +10% = +£1,600/month on current base.
